Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the draft. I pulled a quick pass and attached an ops QA checklist and one-page notes. High level thoughts:

- We can reproduce token-per-session estimates to within ~5% if Vivixa's traffic distribution looks like the sample. The main sensitivity is prompt length variability (you have a 20% wide tail in the sample).
- Caching will reduce token spend primarily on repeated prefixes; we need session identifiers and a 7-day cache TTL to estimate reuse.
- Batching assumptions: for low-latency front-end calls we recommend micro-batching (50–150ms window) which raises GPU utilization and reduces per-token cost by ~12% in our profile; larger batching (200–400ms) helps more on throughput-heavy background jobs.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick ops QA doc that maps MAP rows to Redwood verification checks (I attached ops-validation-checklist.pdf), 2) run a short replay of your sample traffic against a quantized model profile (can do within 48–72h), 3) sync with Michael for procurement-facing numbers.

Can you confirm Michael's availability next Tue/Wed?

—Olga
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
